rv.q: What you get is something stranger, more insidious, and I suspect much more memorable.
Here's your chance to catch him live and in-person, every evening until 24th December as he leads a revival of C.P. Taylor's hard-hitting play GOOD.
Good isn't perfect, but its lessons demand to be understood.
It's a strong framing, and there are striking, resonant messages within this work, but as drama it unsettles when really it should devastate.
